title: Two-Year Follow-Up of 4-mm-Long Implants Used as Distal Support of Full -Arch FDPs Compared to 10 -mm Implants Installed after Sinus Floor Elevation. A Randomized Clinical Trial
authors: Rossi F, Tuci L, Ferraioli L, Ricci E, Suerica A, Botticelli D, Pellegrino G, Felice P. Int J Environ Res Public Health. 2021 Apr 6;18(7):3846. doi: 10.3390/ijerph18073846.
supports: Clinical study from the botiss collprotect (porcine dermis) literature list — the product featured in it, which is not the same as the study being about the product, so check the design and the comparator before citing it as product evidence. Authors' conclusion, verbatim: “Similar results on implant survival rate and marginal bone loss were observed for the short and standard implants, placed in association with a bilateral sinus floor augmentation procedure, used as distal support of a maxillary full -arch FDP. A statistically relevant difference was found only at 12 months after loading between the two groups (p = 0.023)” This records what the paper says, not what a rep may say: the sales wording still has to pass the claim tiers, and a study in one indication licenses nothing in another.
